trust_decision.summary: In assertSecureUrl, a URL whose raw string starts with the lowercase prefix 'data:' is trusted unconditionally and returned before any protocol/size reasoning, and every network-capable client in the library routes its destination URL through that one gate; the fix caps such URLs at 1 MiB at that point.

landing_point.why: The advisory names data: URIs and secureFetch; reading the shared URL gate finds the unconditional 'if (url.startsWith("data:")) return;' early return that the fix extends with a 1 MiB length check.

fix_sites.entry_point: assertSecureUrl (public export, core/src/index.ts:51) reached by secureFetch, createRestClient, createGraphQLClient, createGrpcWebClient, exportToEndpoint
same gate, reached by all five network entry points

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can argue the other routes never use secureFetch and that data: URIs make no network request at all, so only the data: branch in the shared gate needs the cap and the build-time attribute filter (which already blocks javascript:) is a different feature.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Small inline data: URIs must keep being accepted; the pinned tests assert assertSecureUrl('data:text/plain;base64,SGVsbG8=') and ('data:text/html,hello') do not throw, so a fix that rejects every data: URI (rather than capping length) breaks documented, tested behaviour.

O6_input_shapes: lowercase 'data:' URI string, just under and just over the 1 MiB length bound
plain string URL (absolute https, relative / ./ ../, bare filename, empty string)
URL object unwrapped via input.href and Request object unwrapped via input.url before the check
init object carrying a redirect field, spread after the new redirect:'error' default so a caller can override it

O8_uncovered_routes.route: restClient.get/post/put/patch/delete build the URL with buildURL and call fetch() with the default redirect policy, so a validated https URL that redirects to http://internal still egresses
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: This client is not secureFetch and the advisory is about data: URI size; the URL already passes through assertSecureUrl.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different module (core/src/client) from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: graphql query/mutate posts to the configured url with fetch() and the default redirect policy
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Advisory names secureFetch only; the GraphQL client was already covered by the shared gate.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different module (core/src/client) from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: gRPC-Web unary builds baseURL/service/method and calls fetch() with the default redirect policy
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Different transport (binary gRPC-Web), not the fetch wrapper the advisory is about.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different module (core/src/client) from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: exportToEndpoint posts telemetry with fetch() and the default redirect policy, and its surrounding try/catch swallows any throw from the gate
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Telemetry export is best-effort by design (failures are silently ignored), so a validation change there is invisible.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a sendBeacon / keepalive exporter next to exportToEndpoint that posts the same OTLP body on unload
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Telemetry exporters conventionally add a beacon-based transport for unload-safe export; such a sibling would build its own request and never touch assertSecureUrl, and failures are already swallowed by the surrounding catch.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the build-time attribute filter extended with a data:/blob: URL allow-list for img src and a href
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The module already hand-rolls its own URL-scheme rule (blocks javascript: in href/src/style) instead of calling the shared gate, so a maintainer adding data: handling there would naturally write a second, divergent check.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a streaming/SSE or file-upload transport added to the rest client that constructs its own Request and calls fetch directly
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: REST clients grow streaming and upload helpers alongside request(); the fetchInit assembly already sits inline in the client, so a new transport copies it and easily bypasses the shared gate.

O9_family: Server-side request forgery / improper URL validation (CWE-918): URL-scheme allow-list with missing size bound on an allowed scheme

O10_build.toolchain: Node >= 24 for esbuild bundling via core/build.mjs, bun as the test runner/package manager; devDependencies (typescript, esbuild, vite, @asymmetric-effort/nogginlessdom, eslint, playwright) are not vendored in the tree and there is no lockfile at the repo root
O10_build.project_tests: bun test with nogginlessdom preloads (core/package.json:74); the affected area is covered by core/tests/unit/shared/secure-fetch.test.ts, core/tests/unit/security/security-regression.test.ts:190-213, plus core/tests/unit/client/{rest,graphql,protobuf}.test.ts, core/tests/unit/telemetry/metrics.test.ts and core/tests/unit/build/noscript-plugin.test.ts

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject every data: URI outright (or put the length check only inside secureFetch's string path) instead of capping the length in the shared gate, which breaks the legitimate small inline data: URIs the pinned tests require.

out_of_scope_notes: The fix commit bundles four unrelated findings (gql metacharacter injection, CSS expression sanitization, unparseable-URL allow, missing redirect validation) that belong to sibling advisories and to other sinks; only the data: size change is this advisory's fix, and the added PentestReport.md plus the package.json version bump are docs/metadata, not counted as source.
The pinned tree contains prebuilt bundles under assets/ that duplicate library code (e.g. an older secure-fetch copy could exist there); they are build artifacts and were not screened.
